analysis_notes.gap_analysis_detail:
Torah 113 (LM2) is a single-sentence aphorism with no bechina language whatsoever. The full text declares: 'One in whom the Divine name merely flickers — when he does, God forbid, even one thing that is not as it should be in its perfection (meaning: even if there is no trace of sin in it, God forbid, and no complete physical desire — only that he does not do the thing with the utmost perfection of holiness as it truly should be) — it is fitting that his soul should completely expire from the sheer intensity of regret (חֲרָטָה) and shame (בּוּשָׁה).'

The concepts present in the text are: הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ (the Divine name / God's presence), שְׁלֵמוּת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה (the perfection of holiness), נַפְשׁוֹ (the soul), חֲרָטָה (regret), and בּוּשָׁה (shame). None of these are introduced with bechina language. The relationship between acting without full perfection and the experience of shame/regret is causal (eitza): the deficient action produces the shame — one thing leads to the other, they do not share the same essential nature. No missing bechina nodes are identified. The dataset correctly records zero bechina edges for reference 1113.
analysis_notes.evil_mirror_check: No evil polarity is named or described in this Torah. The teaching is addressed entirely at the positive side — a person close to God — and the 'failure' discussed is not the action of the wicked but the imperfection of the very holy. No opposing evil force, no sitra achra language, no evil mirror structure exists here.
